verdicts.quote: “help you establish the API connection through an API key or authentication token.”
verdicts.reason: Vendor help page explicitly lists API key as a supported authentication method; no OAuth is documented. ([pitchbook.com](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Our API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform that requires a standalone contract agreement.”
verdicts.reason: This indicates developers can’t self-serve credentials; you must contact their Direct Data team/sales to get access. ([pitchbook.com](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Call data on all PitchBook entity types including deals, investors, funds, people, limited partners and service providers.”
verdicts.reason: Coverage spans many core objects across the product, consistent with “broad.” ([pitchbook.com](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data/api?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “The PitchBook Data MCP is currently live and available to customers upon request.”
verdicts.reason: Official press release confirms an in-house MCP offering available from PitchBook. ([pitchbook.com](https://pitchbook.com/media/press-releases/pitchbook-launches-an-agentic-platform-assistant-and-new-pitchbook-data-mcp-to-meet-investors-rapidly-evolving-workflow-needs))

Because access to the API (and MCP is “upon request”) isn’t self-serve, Composio would need outreach/contract to ship an integration now. ([pitchbook.com](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api?utm_source=openai))
